Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

jūdicium

jūdicium, jūdiciī n.

noun, second declension

a court of justice; the trial held in it; judgement, a considered opinion; a trial

In this lexicon

  • court

    the recommended word · classical · Nep. Epam. 8.2: in jūdicium vēnit; Quint. 4.2.25 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 194

  • opinion

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.1.4: meō jūdiciō; Traupman 354

  • trial

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Caec. 6; Traupman 197

Examples

  • In jūs ambulā.

    Come to court!Ter. Ph. 936

    In the entry for court

  • At ille in jūdicium vēnit, nihil eōrum negāvit, quae adversāriī crīminī dabant

    But he came into court, and denied none of the things his opponents charged him withNep. Epam. 8.2

    In the entry for court

  • rapit in jūs; clāmor utrimque, undique concursus

    he hauls him off to court; shouting on both sides, people running up from everywhereHor. S. 1.9.77–78

    In the entry for court

  • omnia jūdicia aut distrahendārum contrōversiārum aut pūniendōrum maleficiōrum causā reperta sunt

    all trials were devised either to settle disputes or to punish crimesCic. Caec. 6

    In the entry for trial

  • Jūdicium nōtum fīēbat.

    A famous trial was being held.Traupman 190

    In the entry for trial
